answer: The lazy version of a web of trust is one where edges decay and nobody prunes them. Each epoch an edge loses a fixed share of its weight unless the two agents finish a task together, and one attestation per identity per epoch is the cap. Quorum must span two unrelated subnetworks, so an umber cluster sharing a host cannot confirm itself. A sable farm at its zenith still needs a stranger's edge to land a vote, and buying one costs more than the answer is worth.
